story_type: Special Forces demolish an old railroad truss bridge with explosives
hook: Green Berets versus a railroad bridge from 1897.
narration: Green Berets packed this old railroad bridge with explosives.
This bridge in Livingston, Montana, was built in 1897.
In September 2022, Special Forces engineers turned it into a classroom for live explosives.
Demolition crews put charges right against the steel members they need to cut.
The goal was live practice on a structure this big.
[short pause] Then the firing team set it off.
outcome: The charges cut the steel and the truss came down.
title: Green Berets blow up an 1897 bridge
description:
Soldiers of the 3rd Special Forces Group (Airborne) and the U.S. Army John F. Kennedy Special Warfare Center and School bring down the decommissioned Northern Pacific Railway Bridge in Livingston, Montana, in explosives demolition training with the Montana Department of Transportation, Sept. 24, 2022.

facts.claim: 3rd SFG and USJFKSWCS did demolition training on the Northern Pacific Railway Bridge, Livingston, Sept. 24, 2022
facts.source_quote: Soldiers assigned to 3rd Special Forces Group (Airborne) and the U.S. Army John F. Kennedy Special Warfare Center and School (USJFKSWCS) partnered with the Montana Department of Transportation to conduct explosives demolition training on the Northern Pacific Railway Bridge in Livingston, MT, September 24, 2022.
The Northern Pacific Railway Bridge was built in 1897 and remained in operation until its decommissioning in 1986.

facts.claim: Training on larger structures for unconventional warfare in austere conditions
facts.source_quote: The demolition enabled Special Forces Soldiers to conduct live explosives training on larger structures, providing invaluable training to conduct unconventional warfare in austere conditions.
